subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should isolated cron setup use PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219's bounded derived timeout budget instead of the current fixed 60s watchdog?
rationale: The code fix is narrow, but it changes default availability behavior by allowing pre-runner setup to occupy cron capacity for longer on slow or stuck environments.

options.title: Accept bounded derived timeout
options.body: Merge the existing PR after explicitly accepting that long-timeout isolated cron jobs may wait beyond 60s before setup cleanup and notification.

options.title: Tighten or configure the window
options.body: Ask for a lower cap or an operator-approved config surface if maintainers want more control over stuck setup occupancy.

options.title: Keep the fixed 60s behavior
options.body: Reject the current fix path and leave slow cold-start deployments to fail fast with the existing setup-timeout diagnostic.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded derived timeout
recommendation.body: Merge the existing PR after explicitly accepting that long-timeout isolated cron jobs may wait beyond 60s before setup cleanup and notification.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently changed the same setup-timeout recovery path and are well-positioned to evaluate the no-restart behavior against a longer setup budget.
